newsitem.title: USA: Transportacion Maritima up on payment.
newsitem.headline: Transportacion Maritima up on payment.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) of Transportacion Maritima Mexicana rose Thursday, boosted by news that the company was ready to pay $280 million for its share of a Mexican railway concession, traders said.
ADRs in the transportation company were up 5/8 to 6-1/2, and the 10.64 percent rise put them among leaders on the New York Stock Exchange. Volume was 750,000 ADRs at mid-afternoon.

"The company announced its first payment for the concession. That's what is boosting the stock," a trader said. The prospective payment cleared up uncertainties about financing for the rail project, he said.
Another trader said the stock had been pushed up by a single big buyer. Details were not immediately available.

Transportacion Maritima said this week it would pay the Mexican government $280 million Friday for its 40 percent share of the rail concession in northeast Mexico. The company and Kansas City Southern Industries Inc won the concession last month with a bid of almost $1.4 billion.
